fields.name: DIR
fields.description: Device Identification Number

fields.name: VSA
fields.description: Vertical Sync Active Period – These bits specify the Vsync active period. The Vsync active period is from the Vsync falling edge to rising edge, in terms of Hsync pulses. It is only used in non-burst mode with Sync pulses. Please refer to 9.3 for more details.

fields.name: HSA
fields.description: Horizontal Sync Active Period – These bits specify the Hsync active period. The Hsync active period is from the Hsync falling edge to rising edge, in terms of pclk. It is only used in non-burst mode with Sync pulses. Please refer to 9.3 for more details.

fields.name: VBP
fields.description: Vertical Back Porch Period – These bits specify the vertical back porch period in terms of Hsync pulses. The vertical back porch period depends on the video mode setting. If the mode is non-burst mode with Sync pulses, it is from the Vsync rising edge to the Hsync of the first line of active display. If the mode is non-burst mode with Sync events, it is from the Vsync falling edge to the Hsync of the first line of active display. If the mode is burst mode, it is the same as the non-burst mode with Sync events. Please refer to 9.3 for more details.

fields.name: HBP
fields.description: Horizontal Back Porch Period – These bits specify the horizontal back porch period in terms of pclk. The horizontal back porch period depends on the non-burst mode setting. If the mode is non-burst mode with Sync pulses, it is from the Hsync rising edge to the start of the valid display pixel. If the mode is non-burst mode with Sync events, it is from the Hsync falling edge to the start of the valid display pixel. If the mode is burst mode, it is the same as the non-burst mode with Sync events. Please refer to 9.3for more details.

fields.name: VFP
fields.description: Vertical Front Porch Period – These bits specify the vertical front porch period in terms of Hsync pulses. The vertical front porch period is from the first Hsync after the last line of active display to the next Vsync falling edge. Please refer to 9.3 for more details.

fields.name: HFP
fields.description: Horizontal Front Porch Period – These bits specify the horizontal front porch period in terms of pclk. The horizontal front porch period is from the end of the valid display pixel to the next Hsync falling edge. Please refer to 9.3 for more details.

fields.name: HACT
fields.description: Horizontal Active Period – These bits specify the horizontal active period in terms of pclk. During the horizontal active period, the den signal should always be high. Please refer to 9.3 for more details.

fields.name: VACT
fields.description: Vertical Active Period – These bits specify the vertical active period in terms of Hsync pulses. Please refer to 9.3 for more details.

fields.name: VS_P
fields.description: VS_P – This bit control the polarity of the Vsync pulse input.

fields.name: HS_P
fields.description: HS_P – This bit control the polarity of the Hsync pulse output.

fields.name: PCLK_P
fields.description: PCLK_P – This bit control the polarity of the CM output.

enums.meaning: Data is launch at falling edge, SSD2828 latch data at rising edge
Data is launch at rising edge, SSD2828 latch data at falling edge

fields.name: CBM
fields.description: Compress Burst Mode Control – If the mode is burst and this bit is 1, MIPITX will send video packet in compressed burst mode (i.e. no blanking packet after horizontal sync packet)

fields.name: NVB
fields.description: Non Video Data Burst Mode Control – This bit specifies how non video data will be interleaved with video data transmission in burst mode.

enums.meaning: Non video data will be transmitted during any BLLP period.
Non video data will only be transmitted during vertical blanking period.

fields.name: NVD
fields.description: Non Video Data Transmission Control –This bit specifies how non video data will be interleaved with video data transmission. Please refer to 9.2.1 for more details. The SSD2828 will send non video data (written from the SPI interface) during the vertical blanking period (non burst mode) or any BLLP period in burst mode (depends on NVB setting). The data can be sent either in high speed mode or low power mode. This bit selects which mode to use. If LP mode is selected, the data

fields.name: BLLP
fields.description: BLLP Control – This bit specifies the SSD2828 operation during BLLP period. This bit takes effect only for non burst mode and NVD being 0. When the video mode is burst mode, the SSD2828 will not send any blanking packet during BLLP. It will enter LP mode. When NVD is 1 in non burst mode, the SSD2828 will stay in LP mode after sending the non video data (if there is any), until the BLLP period ends. When NVD is 0 in non burst mode, the SSD2828 will use this bit to decide whether to send blanking packet or enter LP mode after sending non video data (if there is any), until the BLLP period ends. Please note that entering and exiting from LP mode needs more time, as the speed of LP mode is slow. It is the responsibility of the host processor to make sure that the period is long enough to finish the data transfer and the timing of Hsync and Vsync is not affected.

enums.meaning: Blanking packet will be sent during BLLP period.
LP mode will be used during BLLP period.

fields.name: VCS
fields.description: Video Clock Suspend – This bit specifies the clock lane behavior. This bit is only applicable for burst mode. When the video mode is non burst mode, the clock lane will remain in HS mode all the time.

enums.meaning: The clock lane remains in HS mode, when there is no data to transmit.
The clock lane enters LP mode when there is no data to transmit.

fields.name: VM
fields.description: Video Mode – These bits specify the video mode the SSD2828 will use, when RGB interface is selected. Please refer to MIPI DSI for the definition of different modes.

enums.meaning: Non burst mode with sync pulses
Non burst mode with sync events

fields.name: VPF
fields.description: Video Pixel Format – These bits specify the pixel format for video mode.

fields.name: TXD
fields.description: Transmit Disable – This bit specifies whether the SSD2828 will disable the sending of MIPI Packets stored in the buffers. Software can enable TXD, fill out the buffers and then disable it to send all packets out in 1 burst.

fields.name: LPE
fields.description: Long Packet Enable – This bit specifies whether the SSD2828 will send out a Generic Long Write Packet or Generic Short Write Packet when the payload is no more than 2 bytes. It also specifies whether the SSD2828 will send out a DCS Long Write Packet or DCS Short Write Packet when the payload is no more than 1 byte.

fields.name: EOT
fields.description: EOT Packet Enable – This bit specifies whether the SSD2828 will send out the EOT packet at the end of HS transmission or not.

fields.name: ECD
fields.description: ECC CRC Check Disable – This bit specifies whether SSD2828 will perform ECC and CRC checking for the packets received from the MIPI slave.

fields.name: REN
fields.description: Read Enable –This bit specifies whether the next operation is a write or read operation.

fields.name: DCS
fields.description: DCS Enable – This bit specifies whether the packet to be sent is DCS packet or generic packet. This bit applies for both write and read operation.

enums.meaning: Generic packet (The packet can be any one of Generic Long Write, Generic Short Write, Generic Read packet, depending on the configuration.)
DCS packet (The packet can be any one of DCS Long Write, DCS Short Write, DCS Read packet, depending on the configuration.)

fields.name: CSS
fields.description: Clock Source Select – This bit selects the clock source for the PLL. Please refer to 5.2 for the system behavior when the clock source is switched. The CSS setting should be programmed only when PEN is 0. It has no effect when PEN is 1.

fields.name: HCLK
fields.description: HS Clock Disable – This bit controls the clock lane behavior during the reverse direction communication. This bit takes effect only when CKE is 0 and VEN is 0.

fields.name: VEN
fields.description: Video Mode Enable – This bit controls the video mode operation. Only after this bit is set to 1, video mode is enabled. This bit takes effect only when the interface setting is RGB + SPI. Please refer to 0 for the video mode operation.

fields.name: SLP
fields.description: Sleep Mode Enable – This bit controls the sleep mode operation. Please refer to 9.3.2 for the sleep mode operation. When this bit is set to 1, the HS bit will be cleared to 0 automatically.

enums.meaning: Sleep mode is enabled. Only the register interface is active.

fields.name: CKE
fields.description: Clock Lane Enable – This bit controls the clock lane mode when data lane enters LP mode.

enums.meaning: Clock lane will enter LP mode, if it is not in reverse direction communication. Clock lane will follow the setting of HCLK, if it is in reverse direction communication.
Clock lane will enter HS mode for all the cases.

fields.name: HS
fields.description: HS Mode – This bit controls whether the SSD2828 is using HS or LP mode to send data. This bit can be affected by the SLP bit value.

fields.name: VCM
fields.description: Virtual Channel ID for Maximum Return Size Packet – These bits specify the VC ID for the Maximum Return Size Packet sent by SSD2828. This register field is included as the VC ID for this packet might be different from the VC ID for the packets carrying the actual data.

fields.name: VCE
fields.description: Virtual Channel ID for EOT Packet – These bits specify the VC ID for the EOT Packet sent by SSD2828. This register field is included as the VC ID for this packet might be different from the VC ID for the packets carrying the actual data.

fields.name: VC2
fields.description: Virtual Channel ID for SPI Interface – These bits specify the VC ID for the packets written in through the SPI interface, when the interface setting is RGB + SPI This register field is included as the RGB + SPI interface can address two different LCD panels at the same time. The VC ID for the two panels is different.

fields.name: VC1
fields.description: Virtual Channel ID for RGB Interface – These bits specify the VC ID for the packets written in through the RGB interface, when the interface is RGB + SPI

fields.name: SYSD
fields.description: SYS_clk Divider – These bits give the divider value for generating the sys_clk output from the tx_clk or crystal input.

fields.name: SYS_DIS
fields.description: SYS_clk DISable – This bit will shut off the Sys_clk signal output when enabled.

fields.name: PEN
fields.description: PLL Enable – This bit controls the PLL operation.

fields.name: FR
fields.description: Frequency Range – These bits select the range of the output clock. The FR setting should be programmed only when PEN is 0. It has no effect when PEN is 1.

fields.name: MS
fields.description: PLL Divider – These bits specify the PLL pre- divider value, MS. The frequency of the phase detector, f REF is determined by f PRE = f IN MS The input frequency, f IN and phase detector frequency, f REF should be between 5Mhz to 100Mhz. The MS setting should be programmed only when PEN is 0. It has no effect when PEN is 1.

fields.name: NS
fields.description: PLL Multiplier – These bits specify the PLL output frequency multiplier value, NS. The output frequency, f OUT is determined by f OUT = f PRE ∗ NF The NS setting should be programmed only when PEN is 0. It has no effect when PEN is 1.

fields.name: LPD
fields.description: LP Clock Divider – These bits give the divider value for generating the LP mode clock from the byte clock.

fields.name: TDC
fields.description: Transmit Data Count – These bits set the total number of data bytes to be transmitted by the SSD2828 in the next operation. The SSD2828 will use the value in this field to decide what type of packet to send out. The settings of TDC and PST(0xBE) will configure the transfer mode into partition and non-partition mode when the command is 0x2C or 0x3C. Partition mode(TDC > PST) For DCS Long Write packet with DCS command being 0x2C or 0x3C, there is no limit in the maximum number of bytes to be transmitted in 1 write. The PST value can be set to maximum of 4096 bytes. The SSD2828 will auto insert 0x3C command at these boundaries. The maximum MCU speed at the input is 1/12 of the link frequency. Non-Partition mode(TDC <= PST) For DCS Long Write packet with DCS command being 0x2C or 0x3C, the maximum number of bytes to be transmitted in 1 write is 4096 bytes(TDC). In this mode, the PST value is the same or greater than the TDC value. The maximum MCU speed at the input is 1/8 of the link frequency. Please refer to 9.3.1.1 for more details.

fields.name: TDC[31:16] Bit 31-0
fields.description: Transmit Data Count – Please see the description of Packet Size Control Register 1.

fields.name: PST
fields.description: Packet Size Threshold – These bits give the threshold value for partitioning the incoming long packet data into smaller packets. The partitioning only applies to the DCS Long Write packet with DCS command being 0x2C or 0x3C in Command mode(if_sel=1). The payload will be partitioned into multiple packets. The PST represents the threshold in term of bytes. The maximum MCU speed at the input is 1/10 of the link frequency. Please refer to 9.3.1.1 for more details.

fields.name: GPD
fields.description: Generic Packet Drop – This register is not a true register. It is the entry point for the internal buffer. The payload of the generic packets (Generic Short Write, Generic Long Write, and Generic Read) or the command and payload if DCS packet should be written into this register. The SSD2828 will send them out using the corresponding generic or DCS packet. DCS field of CFGR register will be used to determine the data drop into this register is for generic or DCS packet generation. The application processor can treat this register as an FIFO and continuously write data into it. When the interface is 16-bit, the width of this field is 16-bit. When the interface is 8-bit, the width of this field is 8-bit. Since the register is only the entry point of the internal buffer, the application processor is not able to read the data written into the buffer.

fields.name: RST
fields.description: Software Reset - Writing a ‘1’ to this bit will reset the entire module except SSD2828 local register setting. This bit will be cleared after the reset is completed. Wrting a ‘1’ to this bit will cause the MIPI link enters TX stop state immediately and any outgoing MIPI packet will be terminated immediately.

fields.name: COP
fields.description: Cancel Operation – This bit is to cancel the current operation. When this bit is set to 1, the SSD2828 will still finish transmitting the current packet. (Otherwise, the serial link operation will lose sync.) Afterwards, the SSD2828 will stop any further transmission. It will clear its internal buffer such that all the data being written in and not sent out yet will be cleared. It will also bring the state machine to its initial state. Once this process is finished, the COP bit will be automatically set to 0. At the same time, the PO bit of the status register will be set to 1 too. At this stage, there is no data in the internal buffer. The application processor can start a new operation. This operation is not valid in video mode(VEN=1).

fields.name: MRS
fields.description: Maximum Return Size – These bits set the maximum return size of the read response packet returned by the MIPI slave. The SSD2828 will automatically send out the Set Maximum Return Size packet using the value in this field, before every read operation. It informs the MIPI slave about the limit of the SSD2828. The application processor does not need to program the register before every read operation, if the maximum return size does not change. However, the Set Maximum Return Size packet will always be sent.

fields.name: RDC
fields.description: Return Data Count – These bits reflect the number of data bytes received from the MIPI slave read response packet. This register can only be updated by the SSD2828 hardware.

fields.name: AR
fields.description: ACK Response – These bits contain the ACK response from the MIPI slave. The register will be updated when ACK with Error Report packet is received. Otherwise, the value will be set to 0. The bits in this register follow the definition in MIPI DSI. This register can only be updated by the SSD2828 hardware.

fields.name: IBC
fields.description: Ignore Bus Contention – This bit is to detect bus contention reported by the Analog Phy. If this bit is disabled, whenever bus contention is detected, the state machine will ignore it and continue sending new packet if available. If this bit is enabled, the state machine will halt further transmission.

enums.meaning: Detect Bus Contention from Analog Phy
Ignore Bus Contention detected by Analog Phy

fields.name: RT
fields.description: Reset Trigger – This bit is to send a Reset Trigger Message. When this bit is set to 1, the SSD2828 will send a Reset Trigger Message. It is recommended to enter LP mode and send this trigger message. If this bit is programmed during vertical active data is being sent on MIPI link, the reset trigger will be delayed to next vertical blanking period so that the reset trigger message will not disturb the video timing on the MIPI link. Once the Reset Trigger Message is sent out, RT bit will be automatically set to 0.

fields.name: RTB
fields.description: Register Triggered BTA – This bit automatically perform Bus Turnaround(BTA) when link is not used. When bus is returned back from the slave, the link will remains in Low Power state until a new request come in where HS bit determination the transfer mode.

enums.meaning: Automatically perform BTA when link is available. In video mode, it will be sent at the next vertical blanking period.

fields.name: FBC
fields.description: Force Bus Contention – This bit controls whether to force a bus contention on the data lane. This bit will be changed to 0, after the bus contention is not detected.

enums.meaning: Drive the data lane to LP11 to force a bus contention.

fields.name: FBT
fields.description: perform automatic BTA after previous BTA so as to get the TE response from MIPI slave.

enums.meaning: Perform automatic BTA after previous BTA

fields.name: FBW
fields.description: Force BTA After Write – This bit controls whether to automatically generate a BTA after a write operation. It is only valid for write operation. After performing BTA, the bus authority has been passed to the MIPI slave. The SSD2828 is not able to send any data to the MIPI slave before the bus authority is passed back. It is the responsibility of the application processor to check the status of the bus before sending any data.

enums.meaning: Not BTA after the next write packet.
Automatically perform BTA after the next write packet.

fields.name: CBEE
fields.description: Command Buffer Empty Enable – This bit enables the mapping of CBE interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: CBAE
fields.description: Command Buffer Available Enable – This bit enables the mapping of CBA interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: MLEE
fields.description: MCU Long Buffer Empty Enable – This bit enables the mapping of MLE interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: MLAE
fields.description: MCU Long Buffer Available Enable – This bit enables the mapping of MLA interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: PLSE
fields.description: PLL Lock Status Enable – This bit enables the mapping of the PLS interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: LPTOE
fields.description: LP RX Time Out Enable – This bit enables the mapping of the LPTO interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: HSTOE
fields.description: HS TX Time Out Enable – This bit enables the mapping of the HSTO interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: ARRE
fields.description: ACK Response Ready Enable – This bit enables the mapping of ARR interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: BTARE
fields.description: BTA Response Enable – This bit enables the mapping of the BTAR interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: POE
fields.description: Packet Operation Enable – This bit enables the mapping of the PO interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: RDRE
fields.description: Read Data Ready Enable – This bit enables the mapping of the RDR interrupt to the int pin.

fields.name: CBE
fields.description: Command Buffer Empty – This bit reflects the status of the internal command buffer of the SPI interface. If the command buffer is empty, this bit will be set to 1. The application processor can write up to the maximum size of the command buffer.

enums.meaning: The command buffer is not empty.

fields.name: CBA
fields.description: Command Buffer Available – This bit reflects the status of the internal command buffer of the SPI interface. If the command buffer is not full, this bit will be set to 1. The application processor can write at least 1 packet to the command buffer.

enums.meaning: The command buffer is full. 1 – The command buffer is not full.

fields.name: CST
fields.description: Clock Lane Status – This bit reflects the status at the MIPI Clock lane.

enums.meaning: Clock lane is not in LP-11.

fields.name: DST
fields.description: Data Lane Status – This bit reflects the status at the MIPI Data lane.

enums.meaning: Data lane is not in LP-11.

fields.name: MLE
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: MLA
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: PLS
fields.description: PLL Lock Status – This bit reflects the status of the PLL. Before the PLL is locked, the whole system is running at the reference clock input of the PLL, as the PLL has no output before getting lock. Hence, the application processor must access the registers using slow speed.

fields.name: LPTO
fields.description: LP RX Time Out – This bit reflects the status of the LP RX timer.

enums.meaning: The LP RX timer has expired. 1 – The LP RX timer has not expired.

fields.name: HSTO
fields.description: HS TX Time Out – This bit reflects the status of the HS TX timer.

enums.meaning: The HS TX timer has expired. 1 – The HS TX timer has not expired.

fields.name: ATR
fields.description: ACK Trigger Response – This bit reflects whether the ACK trigger message has been received or not.

enums.meaning: ACK trigger message has not been received.
ACK trigger message has been received.

fields.name: ARR
fields.description: ACK Response Ready – This bit reflects whether the ACK response has been received or not. The ACK response can be an ACK trigger message or ACK with Error Report packet.

fields.name: BTAR
fields.description: BTA Response – This bit reflects the data lane status after SSD2828 has made a BTA.

enums.meaning: The MIPI slave has not passed the lane authority back.
The MIPI slave has passed the lane authority back.

fields.name: PO
fields.description: Packet Operation – This bit reflects whether the SSD2828 is ready to take in more data from the application processor.

fields.name: RDR
fields.description: Read Data Ready – This bit reflects whether the data from the MIPI slave is ready for read by the application processor. This bit is valid only during the read operation. This bit will be automatically cleared when all the received data are read out.

fields.name: CRCE
fields.description: CRC Error – This bit reflects the status of CRC checking for the packets received from the MIPI slave. The status is valid only when the ECD bit is set to 0. Once a CRC error occurs, this bit will be set to 1. It will remain as 1 until the application processor writes 1 to clear it.

enums.meaning: No CRC error since this bit is cleared
At least 1 CRC error since this bit is cleared

fields.name: ECCE2
fields.description: ECC Multi Bit Error – This bit reflects the status of ECC checking for the packets received from the MIPI slave. The status is valid only when the ECD bit is set to 0. Once an ECC multi-bit error occurs, this bit will be set to 1. It will remain as 1 until the application processor writes 1 to clear it.

enums.meaning: No ECC multi-bit error since this bit is cleared
At least 1 ECC multi-bit error since this bit is cleared

fields.name: ECCE1
fields.description: ECC Single Bit Error – This bit reflects the status of ECC checking for the packets received from the MIPI slave. The status is valid only when the ECD bit is set to 0. Once an ECC single-bit error occurs, this bit will be set to 1. It will remain as 1 until the application processor writes 1 to clear it.

enums.meaning: No ECC single-bit error since this bit is cleared
At least 1 ECC single-bit error since this bit is cleared

fields.name: SO
fields.description: Command Buffer Overflow – This bit reflects the status of internal command buffer of the SPI interface. If the command buffer has overflowed, this bit will be set to 1. It will remain as 1 until the application processor writes 1 to clear it.

fields.name: MLO
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: CONT
fields.description: data lane contention detector.

fields.name: VMM
fields.description: VC Mis Match – This bit reflects whether there is a mismatch between the VC ID transmitted by the SSD2828 and the VC ID received from the MIPI slave

fields.name: HZD
fields.description: HS Zero Delay – These bits specifies the number of nibble clock for HS zero delay period T_HS-ZERO.

fields.name: HPD
fields.description: HS Prepare Delay – These bits specifies the number of nibble clock for HS prepare delay period T_HS-PREPARE.

fields.name: CZD
fields.description: CLK Zero Delay – These bits specifies the number of nibble clock for CLK zero delay period T_CLK-ZERO.

fields.name: CPD
fields.description: CLK Prepare Delay – These bits specifies the number of nibble clock for CLK prepare delay period T_CLK-PREPARE.

fields.name: CPED
fields.description: CLK Pre Delay – These bits specifies the number of nibble clock for CLK pre delay period T_CLK-PER.

fields.name: CPTD
fields.description: CLK Post Delay – These bits specifies the number of nibble clock for CLK post delay period T_CLK-POST.

fields.name: CTD
fields.description: CLK Trail Delay – These bits specifies the number of nibble clock for CLK trail delay period T_CLK-TRAIL.

fields.name: HTD
fields.description: HS Trail Delay – These bits specifies the number of nibble clock for HS trail delay period T_HS-TRAIL. Please note that the minimum value for the T_HS- _L is 3.

fields.name: WUD
fields.description: Wake Up Delay – These bits specifies the number of clock cycles for wake up delay period T_WAKEUP. The delay is used to wake up the MIPI slave from ULPS state. The clock is the low power clock.

fields.name: TGO
fields.description: TA Go Delay – These bits specifies the number of T_LPX for TA go delay period T_TA-GO.

fields.name: TGET
fields.description: TA Get Delay – These bits specifies the number of T_LPX for TA get delay period T_TA-GET.

fields.name: HTT
fields.description: HS TX Timer – These bits specify the HS TX timer timeout value. PLL reference clock is used to increment an internal timer. The timer starts when the SSD2828 enters HS transmit mode. When the SSD2828 exits from HS transmit mode, the timer will be reset. If the timer expires before the end of HS transmission, the SSD2828 will signal an error and switch to LP mode to continue the transmission. At the same time, the HS bit will be cleared to 0. Software intervention is required so that the SSD2828 can go back to proper HS transmission mode.

fields.name: HTT
fields.description: Please see the description of HS TX Timer Register 1

fields.name: LRT
fields.description: LP RX Timer – These bits specify the LP RX timer timeout value. PLL reference clock is used to increment an internal timer. The timer starts when the SSD2828 enters LP receive mode. When the SSD2828 exits from LP receive mode, the timer will be reset. If the timer expires before exiting from LP receive mode, the SSD2828 will signal an error and switch to LP transmit mode. The DPHY will drive the data lane to LP11 state. Software intervention is required so that any possible error could be cleared.

fields.name: LRT
fields.description: Please see the description of LP RX Timer Register 1

fields.name: TER
fields.description: TE Response – This bit reflects whether a TE response has been received or not. Once a TE response is received, this bit will be set to 1. At the same time, the output te signal will go high. The host processor can write 1 to clear this bit. Once the bit is cleared, the te signal will go low.

fields.name: RRA
fields.description: Register Read Address – These bits specify the address of the register to be read through the SPI interface, when the interface is SPI 8-bit (either 3 wire or 4 wire).

fields.name: LOCK
fields.description: LOCK – These bits specify the PLL lock range in term of PLL reference frequency, f FIN . The maximum PLL lock period is 500us and the default setting assumed the reference clock, f FIN is 10Mhz from tx_clk. The LOCK setting should be programmed only when PEN is 0. It has no effect when PEN is 1.

fields.name: TM/FL0
fields.description: Test Mode – These bits selects whether to inject CRC/ECC error for the outgoing streams. They are used for debugging purpose only. They should be set to 00 in normal mode! Force Lane 0 – These bits are valid when FLM is 1. During this mode, user can write Low Power value to the MIPI lane 0 data using these bits. SSD2828 will not respond to the normal request through RGB or SPI interface. FL0[1] controls MIPI_DP0 and FL0[0] controls MIPI_DN0.

fields.name: EIC
fields.description: Error Injection Control – These bits controls the position of the error being injected for testing. It is only applicable when TM is 01.

fields.name: FLM
fields.description: Force Lane Mode – This bit enable user to write to FL0 bits to directly control the analog lane DP0 and DP1. The lane should be in Low Power mode(HS=0) when write using FL0.

fields.name: PNB
fields.description: Packet Number in Blanking Period – These bits controls the number of packet to send during video mode blanking period.

fields.name: END
fields.description: Endianess – Internal test only. Default as 0

fields.name: CO
fields.description: Color Order – This bit specifies the order of the color component in the pixel. During command mode transmission, this bit takes effect only when the IFS bit is 1 and the transmitted packet is DCS write memory packet, 0x2C or 0x3C. During video mode transmission, this bit must be set to 1 so as to follow the MIPI DSI specification.

enums.meaning: RGB. R is in the higher
BGR. B is in the higher

fields.name: TEC
fields.description: TE Count – These bits determines the pulse width of the output te signal. A counter will be started after the TE signal goes to 1. When the counter reaches the value in TEC field, the te signal will be set to 0. The counter uses the PLL reference clock to do counting.

fields.name: D3_DELAY_SEL[3:2]
fields.description: Data lane 3 DELAY SELect[3:2] – These bits control the delay for serializer output to the HS transmitter.

fields.name: D1_DELAY_SEL
fields.description: Data lane 1 DELAY SELect – These bits control the delay for serializer output to the HS transmitter.

fields.name: D3_DELAY_SEL[1:0]
fields.description: Data lane 3 DELAY SELect[1:0] – These bits control the delay for serializer output to the HS transmitter.

fields.name: D0_DELAY_SEL
fields.description: Data lane 0 DELAY SELect – These bits control the delay for serializer output to the HS transmitter.

fields.name: HSTX_Z
fields.description: High Speed Transmit Trimming control – These bits control the trimming for output impedance control.

fields.name: LPTXDS
fields.description: Low Power TX Drive strength Selection – These bits control the drive strength for the TX in low power mode.

fields.name: HSTX_DS

fields.name: IAS
fields.description: Interrupt Active State – This bit selects the polarity of the int pin at the chip IO. Write to this bit is only valid when all the enable bits in the Interrupt Control Registers(0xC5) are 0.

fields.name: VBN
fields.description: Vertical Front Porch Non Video Data Window These fields specify the number of vertical back porch counting backward from the first vertical active line in which non-video data is not allowed to be sent via MIPI link. This field is only valid when VEN is 1 and the interface setting is RGB + SPI. This field should not larger than VBP. If it is larger, the internal logic will cap this field to VBP.

fields.name: VFN
fields.description: Vertical Back Porch Non Video Data Window These fields specify the number of vertical front porch from the last vertical active line in which non-video data is not allowed to be sent via MIPI link. This field is only valid when VEN is 1 and the interface setting is RGB + SPI. This field should not larger than VFP. If it is larger, the internal logic will cap this field to VFP.

fields.name: LS
fields.description: Lane Select – These bits define the number of lane to be used for SSD2828.

fields.name: HED
fields.description: HS Exit Delay – These bits specifies the number of nibble clock for HS exit delay period for data and clock lane.

fields.name: WDBV
fields.description: Write Display Brightness Value – These bits control the brightness setting.

fields.name: GAM18
fields.description: Gamma 18 – This bit controls gamma 18 select.

fields.name: BL
fields.description: BackLight Control – This bit controls the backlight on/off at BC line.

fields.name: DD
fields.description: Display Dimming – This bit controls the display dimming feature.

fields.name: BCTR
fields.description: Brightness Control – This bit controls the On/Off state of the Brightness Control block.

fields.name: BP_MODE
fields.description: BP MODE – These bits control the Brightness Preservation of the CABC.

fields.name: CABC_ EN
fields.description: CABC ENable – This bit enable the CABC feature. This bit is valid only when if_sel is 0.

fields.name: PWM_PS
fields.description: PWM PreScale – These bits control the PWM signal frequency.

fields.name: BCB_PS
fields.description: BCB PreScale – These bits control the number of iternation per second carried out by the BCB unit.

fields.name: CABC_MB
fields.description: CABC Minimum Brightness – These bits control the CABC Minimum Brightness level.

fields.name: VGA_SEL
fields.description: VGA SELect – These bits select the type of resolution of the RGB frame. Panel resolutions need not be matched exactly. For example, "0111" will work for any panel with 384000 pixels (+/- 15%). In other words, the range is 326400 to 441600 pixels. Hence, 800x480, 480x800, 512x750 and 750x512 will be supported by VGA_SEL= "0111".

fields.name: BCL
fields.description: Brightness Control Line – This bit is the pulse width modulation signal output to control external backlight power source. This output is used for Architecture I.

fields.name: RDBV
fields.description: Read Display Brightness Value – These bits show the brightness value of the CABC. This output is used for Architecture II.

fields.name: ENC_LW
fields.description: ENCoder LineWidth – These bits define the input line width of the Encoder input.

fields.name: ENC_MO DE
fields.description: ENCoder Mode – This bit select the Smartlink Encoder mode. This bit is valid only when if_sel is 0.

fields.name: ENC_EN
fields.description: ENCoder ENable – This bit enable the Smartlink Encoder feature. This bit is valid only when if_sel is 0.

fields.name: VSD
fields.description: VSync Delay – These bits control the internal pipeline delay of the Vsync input.

fields.name: HSD
fields.description: HSync Delay – These bits control the internal pipeline delay of the Hsync input.

fields.name: TRIM_ DONE
fields.description: TRIMming DONE – This bit indicates if the trimming process is done.

fields.name: TRIM_ PASS
fields.description: TRIMming PASS – This bit indicates if the trimming process is successful. It is valid when bit 15 is set to 1.

fields.name: XORC_ DONE
fields.description: XOR Calibration DONE – This bit indicates if the trimming process is done. This bit will be cleared when read.

fields.name: XORC_ SEL
fields.description: XOR Calibration SELect – This bit select the internal byte data for calibration to be 8’hAA or 8’h55.

fields.name: XORC_ EN
fields.description: XOR Calibration ENable – This bit starts the internal XOR calibration process and when the calibration is done, this bit will be auto clear and the status bits at bit 13 indicates that the calibration process is done.

fields.name: VBIST_ SRT
fields.description: Video BIST StaRT – This bit starts the video bist process. Once clear, the video bist engine will stop at the frame boundary. The software should wait for at least 1 frame time before disabling the VBIST_EN bit.

fields.name: VBIST_ EN
fields.description: Video BIST ENable – This bit enables the video bist function. The SSD2828 will automatically send the color, red, green, blue, black and white repeatedly base on current setting. This bit should be 0 in normal mode.

fields.name: TRIM_EN
fields.description: TRIMming ENable – This bit enables the auto trimming process and when the trimming is done, this bit will be auto clear and the status bits at bit 14 and bit 15 indicates if the trimming process is successful.

fields.name: TRIM_CMD[7:4]
fields.description: TRIMming CoMmanD – These bits define the upper 4 bits of the command header byte to be used in auto-trimming mode, when TRIM_EN=1, where SSD2828 send out a read request to the MIPI receiver.

fields.name: TRIM_CMD[3:0]/XORC_FILTER[3:0]
fields.description: TRIMming CoMmanD – These bits define the lower 4 bits of the command header byte to be used in auto-trimming mode, when TRIM_EN=1, where SSD2828 send out a read request to the MIPI receiver. When XORC_EN=1, these bits define the filter to qualify the XOR calibration pulse width.

fields.name: DELAY_A_0

fields.name: DELAY_A_3
fields.description: DELAY A for lane 3 – These bits provide the status of the XOR calibration results when XORC_SEL is set to 0.

fields.name: DELAY_A_2
fields.description: DELAY A for lane 2 – These bits provide the status of the XOR calibration results when XORC_SEL is set to 0.

fields.name: DELAY_B_1

fields.name: DELAY_B_0
fields.description: DELAY B for lane 0 – These bits provide the status of the XOR calibration results when XORC_SEL is set to 1.

fields.name: DELAY_B_3
fields.description: DELAY B for lane 3 – These bits provide the status of the XOR calibration results when XORC_SEL is set to 1.

fields.name: DELAY_B_2
fields.description: DELAY B for lane 2 – These bits provide the status of the XOR calibration results when XORC_SEL is set to 1.

fields.description: DELAY C for lane 1 – These bits provide the status of the average XOR calibration results from DELAY_A_1 and DELAY_B_1.

fields.name: DELAY_C_0
fields.description: DELAY C for lane 0 – These bits provide the status of the average XOR calibration results from DELAY_A_0 and DELAY_B_0.

fields.name: DELAY_C_3
fields.description: DELAY C for lane 3 – These bits provide the status of the average XOR calibration results from DELAY_A_3 and DELAY_B_3.

fields.name: DELAY_C_2
fields.description: DELAY C for lane 2 – These bits provide the status of the average XOR calibration results from DELAY_A_2 and DELAY_B_2.

fields.name: DEC_XO R_E
fields.description: DECoder XOR Enable – This bit enables the XOR function in the analog when Bit[0] is set. This bit is used for internal testing and should be programmed to 0 for normal use.

fields.name: DEC_FB_ E
fields.description: DECoder FeedBack Enable – This bit enables the Decoder function in the analog when Bit[0] is set. This bit is used for internal testing and should be programmed to 0 for normal use.

fields.name: D3_FB_E
fields.description: D3 FeedBack Enable – This bit enables the XOR Feedback Tuning for lane 3 when Bit[0] is set. This bit is used for internal testing and should be programmed to 0 for normal use.

fields.name: D2_FB_E
fields.description: D2 FeedBack Enable – This bit enables the XOR Feedback Tuning for lane 2 when Bit[0] is set. This bit is used for internal testing and should be programmed to 0 for normal use.

fields.name: D1_FB_E
fields.description: D1 FeedBack Enable – This bit enables the XOR Feedback Tuning for lane 1 when Bit[0] is set. This bit is used for internal testing and should be programmed to 0 for normal use.

fields.name: D0_FB_E
fields.description: D0 FeedBack Enable – This bit enables the XOR Feedback Tuning for lane 0 when Bit[0] is set.

fields.name: XOR_TU NE_EN
fields.description: XOR TUNE ENable – This bit enables the XOR Feedback Tuning when Bit[0] is set. This bit is used for internal testing and should be programmed to 0 for normal use.

fields.name: REG_ CTR
fields.description: Analog REGister ConTRol – This bit enable the control of the XOR feedback tuning through register Bit[7:1] or through Analog Test mode 4. This bit is used for internal testing and should be programmed to 0 for normal use.

fields.name: RD
fields.description: Read Data – This register is not a true register. It is the entry point for the internal buffer. It is used to read the data returned by the MIPI slave. The application processor can treat this register as an FIFO and continuously read data from it. When the interface is 16-bit, the width of this field is 16-bit. When the interface is 8-bit, the width of this field is 8-bit. The read of this register is only valid when the RDY bit is 1. In other words, only when the data returned by the MIPI slave is received, the application processor can read this register to get return data.
